scope: Theorem 1.2 of the manuscript “Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights” (preprints/Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3dae0156982e5d20), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed x ∈ [1/ √ 2, 1] there exists σ(x) ∈ (0, ∞), independent of D and of the inside approximation in Definition 1.1, such that hδ σ(x) =⇒ ΦD in D′ (D). In particular, the fields are tight as random distributions and, for every k ≥ 1 and f1, . . . , fk ∈ C∞ c (D), the vector (hδ(fi)/σ(x))k i=1 converges to (ΦD(fi))k i=1. All mixed moments of these vectors converge.
